cards.title: input() gives text
cards.body: `input()` always gives back text, even when the user types digits. Adding two pieces of text glues them together.
cards.code:
a = input()
b = input()
print(a + b)

hi.title: input() text deta hai
hi.body: `input()` hamesha text hi deta hai, chahe user digits type kare. Do text ko add karne par woh bas jud jaate hain.

cards.title: int() makes a number
cards.body: Wrap `input()` in `int()` to turn the text into a whole number. Now the maths works.
cards.code:
a = int(input())
b = int(input())
print(a - b)

hi.title: int() number banata hai
hi.body: `input()` ko `int()` mein wrap karo, toh text whole number ban jaata hai. Ab maths sahi chalega.

cards.title: print() shows numbers too
cards.body: `print()` works with numbers and with whole calculations.

hi.title: print() numbers bhi dikhata hai
hi.body: `print()` numbers aur poori calculations ke saath bhi kaam karta hai.

cards.title: Spot the bug
cards.body: It should add two numbers, but it crashes. The error points at line 3: tap the line that really causes it.
cards.code:
a = int(input())
b = input()
print(a + b)

bug.fix: `input()` gives text, so `b` is text and `a + b` can't add it to a number. Line 2 needs `int(input())`, like line 1.

hi.title: Bug dhoondo
hi.body: Isse do numbers add karne chahiye, par yeh crash ho jaata hai. Error line 3 dikhata hai: us line par tap karo jo asal mein problem hai.
hi.fix: `input()` text deta hai, isliye `b` text hai aur `a + b` use number ke saath add nahi kar sakta. Line 1 ki tarah line 2 ko bhi `int(input())` chahiye.

check.question: What does this print?
check.explanation: Both values are strings in quotes, so + joins them into 44.

hi.question: Yeh kya print karega?
hi.explanation: Dono values quotes mein strings hain, isliye + unhe jodkar 44 bana deta hai.
